Washington, Thursday, January 21, 1954
TITLE 3— THE PRESIDENT
EXECUTIVE ORDER 10512
Revocation  op  E x e c u t iv e O rder  N o.

WHEREAS by Executive Order No.  
9 0 4 7  of January 30,1942, certain officers 
and employees in the executive branch  
of the Government were exempted from  
automatic separation from the service  
under the provisions of the Civil Service 
Retirement Act of May 29, 1930, as  
amended, for an indefinite period of time 
not extending beyond the duration of  
their appointment or term of service;  
and
WHEREAS, in my judgment, the pub-  
lie interest no longer requires the exemp­
tion of any of such officer or employee 
from automatic separation from the  
service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 204 of 
the act of June 30,1932, 47 Stat. 382,404, 
and as President of the United States, it 
is ordered that the said Executive Order 
No. 9047 be, and it is hereby, revoked.
This order shall become effective at  
the close of business on March 31, 1954.
D w ig h t D. E is e n h o w e r -
The  W h ite H o use,
January 19, 1954.
IP . R. Doc. 54-461; Filed, Jan. 20, 1954;
10:29 a. m.j
EXECUTIVE ORDER 10513
Designating  C ertain  O fficers  T o A ct 
as S ecretary  of  L abor
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by section 179 of the Revised Statutes of 
the United States (5 U. S. C. 6) and sec­
tion 301 of title 3 of the United States  
Code, it is ordered as follows:
I hereby authorize and direct the As­
sistant Secretaries of Labor and the So­
licitor of Labor, jn the order designated
17 P. R. 629; 3 CFR, 1943 Cum. Supp.
as hereinafter provided, to perform the  
duties of the office of the Secretary of  
Labor in case of the absence, sickness,  
resignation, or death of both the Secre­
tary of Labor and the Under Secretary of  
Labor.
The Assistant Secretaries of Labor and  
the Solicitor of Labor shall act as Secre­
tary of Labor as herein provided (1) in  
such order as the Secretary of Labor (or  
the Under Secretary when acting as Sec­
retary) may by order designate from  
time to time, or (2) if no such designation 
order is in effect at the time, in the order 
of the respective dates of their commis­
sions, or in the event that two or more  
of their commissions bear the same date,  
in the order in which they shall have  
taken their oath of office.
This order supersedes Executive Order  
No. 9968 of June 17,1948, entitled “Desig­
nation of Certain Officers To Act as Sec­
retary of Labor.”
D w ig h t D . Eise n h o w e r
T h e W h it e H o u se,
January 19,1954.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The operative command revokes Executive Order 2414 of June 30, 1916 and the order becomes effective at the close of business on December 31, 1953. The revocation is a one-time act, performed when it took effect, so the clause was spent at the close of business on December 31, 1953, a date earlier than the signing date 1954-01-19 and the filing date 1954-01-20, which are the alternative readings. No later order is held that postpones, amends or revokes this order.

research_rationale:
EO 10514 (signed 1954-01-19 by Dwight D. Eisenhower; filed 1954-01-20, 10:29 a.m.; 19 FR 369, Federal Register of January 21, 1954 per the held source record) is read in full from the registered text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10514.txt; its number, title and date agree with the census register. The dossier split the order into a lead clause and a stray clause holding only the last year of the effective-date sentence; I replace them with one clause (characters 3415 to 3970 of the registered file), which holds the whole order: under the act of March 12, 1914 (38 Stat. 305) and on the Secretary of the Interior's recommendation, it revokes Executive Order 2414 of June 30, 1916 (hospital-service regulations for the construction and operation of the Government railway in Alaska, now the Alaska Railroad), and the order becomes effective at the close of business on December 31, 1953. First end: the revocation is a one-time act with a stated effective moment, so it was performed, and the clause spent, at the close of business on December 31, 1953. That date precedes the signing date (1954-01-19) and the filing date (1954-01-20); the order's own effective-date sentence is what fixes the end, and the signing and filing dates are the alternative readings a reviewer may weigh. The consequence, that Executive Order 2414 no longer applies, is a completed result and not a continuing command. Later instruments: a scan of every held order text for the bare number 10514 found only the order's own copies, the earlier orders printed in the same issue and unrelated page numbers; none amends, postpones or revokes it. Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121, citations of the order by number, edition through 2026-10-09, no hit), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk, citations by number, no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes for 1937 onward plus operative sentences of saved order texts).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Nothing held amends, postpones or revokes the order; its stated effective moment is the first end. The signing and filing dates are later than that moment and are disclosed as alternative readings.","independent_command_check":"The effective-date sentence only dates the revocation; the order contains no other command.","savings_check":"None stated; the revocation is a performed act with no continuing command.","scope_check":"One clause after correcting the dossier's split of the effective-date sentence; no partial effect is held or found."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order has no savings, exception or pending-matter wording. Its result, the revocation of Executive Order 2414 from the close of business on December 31, 1953, is a completed act with no continuing command.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sentence amends Executive Order 10334 so that Frederick C. Mayer's exemption from compulsory retirement runs until December 31, 1954 instead of for an indefinite period. No held order extends, renews or revokes the exemption or this order before or after that date.

research_rationale:
EO 10569 (signed 1954-10-05 by Dwight D. Eisenhower; filed 1954-10-07, 10:12 a.m.; 19 FR 6493, Federal Register of October 8, 1954 per the held source record) is read in full from the registered text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10569.txt; its number, title and date agree with the census register. The dossier inventory lists eleven clauses, but ten of them are Civil Service Commission notices printed after the order on the same Federal Register page (subsections (k), (b) and (e) of the exceptions from the competitive service) and are not part of this order. I replace the inventory with one clause, characters 1180 to 1563 of the registered file: the sentence that amends Executive Order 10334 of March 26, 1952, which exempted Frederick C. Mayer, organist and choirmaster at the United States Military Academy, from compulsory retirement for an indefinite period, by substituting the words until December 31, 1954 for the words for an indefinite period of time in its last paragraph, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932. The two recitals command nothing. First end: the amended exemption runs until December 31, 1954. Following the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on until-dates, the end is recorded as that stated date, inclusive (the order runs through the end of December 31, 1954); the exclusive reading is the alternative, under which the exemption ends when December 31, 1954 begins. The amending act itself was performed when the order took effect; the lifecycle of this order is the period it fixed for the exemption. Later instruments: a scan of every held order text for the bare number 10569 found only the order's own copies and unrelated page numbers; a scan for the appointee's name found Executive Order 10334, the recitals of this order, and no later order extending or renewing the exemption; the person-name machine search found no hit. Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121, citations of the order by number, edition through 2026-10-09, no hit), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk, citations by number, no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes for 1937 onward plus operative sentences of saved order texts). I also adopted the held-text person-name search.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Nothing held amends, revokes or shortens the order or the amended exemption before December 31, 1954. The appointee could have left service earlier, but no held source says so and the stated date is the order's own end.","independent_command_check":"The only command is the amendment, which sets the end of the exemption; the effective-date wording of the neighboring notices does not belong to this order.","savings_check":"None stated; after the end date no exemption continues.","scope_check":"One clause after correcting the dossier inventory, which had added ten neighboring Civil Service Commission notices to the order. The amended exemption is not partial."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order has no savings, pending-matter or continuing-effect wording. After December 31, 1954 the exemption it fixed no longer applies, and nothing in the order preserves any effect past that date; Executive Order 10334 is a separate order whose own exemption the amendment limited.

WHEREAS by Executive Order No. 
10334 of March 26, 1952, Frederick C. 
Mayeiv organist and choirmaster at the 
United States Military Academy, was 
exempted from compulsory retirement 
for an indefinite period of time; and 
WHEREAS, in my judgment, it is ap­
propriate and in the public interest that 
the said Executive Order be amended as 
provided below;
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 204 of 
the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 404 < 5 
U. S. C. 715a), it is ordered that Execu­
tive Order No. 10334 of March 26, 1952, 
be, and it is hereby, amended by substi­
tuting for the words “for an indefinite 
period of time”, occurring, in the last 
paragraph thereof, the phrase “until 
December 31, 1954”.
